Title: Support barrier-free accessibility
Details: From mid-2025, websites and apps will be legally required to be barrier-free. This is regulated by the Barrier-Free Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) implements the EU directive of the European Accessibility Act (EAA) so that standardised rules on accessibility apply throughout Europe. The regulations are based on the European standard EN 301 549, which in turn is largely based on the international guidelines for accessible web content (WCAG). e.g. sufficient contrast between foreground and background colour, links and buttons operable via the keyboard, screen reader compatibility of a website, etc. Even if the website offers this accessibility on its live site, there is still a risk that the variant of an experiment or personalisation will not fulfil it. Such a design can have legal consequences and penalties. There are various features in Kameleoon that check for accessibility when changes are made. The contrast check of colours in new editors is a first step and a good example of this. The customer wants more AI in the Graphic Editor. There is currently support for the barrier-free accessibility of headings, for example. One suggestion is that the AI should support where it is best to place the element. A possible suggestion is that the place where the element is best placed is highlighted in color. great differentiators with enterprise groups.
Tags: Owner: Ivan Kulagin, Request by: melanie.kaempf@burda.com, Request by: christian.buntrock@freenet.ag, Request by: echarmat@kameleoon.com, Freenet, Burda Verlag, Kameleoon

Title: Support Custom Bucketing Key
Details: A custom bucketing key will allow you to control how users are consistently assigned to variations based on a user-defined identifier rather than the default one (visitor code). This is especially useful when your customers such as agencies (or certain applications) need to group users differently than the default logic for example, by account ID, session ID, device ID, or any other relevant key in your business logic. By using a custom bucketing key, you ensure that the same entity (e.g., a company or group) always gets the same variation, even if individual users change or switch devices. Its also helpful in B2B contexts where features should be rolled out at the account level, not the user level. This flexibility gives you greater targeting precision, consistency, and control in your rollouts and experiments.
